name: Identify common trees
blurb: Fifteen local species, identified in all four seasons — including in winter, when there are no leaves and most people are lost.
gear: A regional tree guide with a key
steps: Start with the ten commonest species where you live and learn them by leaf first.
Learn to use the whole tree: bark texture, branching pattern, buds, overall silhouette and habitat.
Learn the big divisions: opposite versus alternate branching, compound versus simple leaves, needle arrangement in conifers.
Learn winter identification by twig and bud, which is the real test and the most useful skill.
Visit the same trees monthly through a year and photograph them.
Learn the useful associations: which trees indicate wet ground, which indicate old woodland.
tips: Opposite branching narrows the field enormously in temperate regions — very few families have it.
Bark changes dramatically with age. Learn both young and mature versions of each species.
proof: You identify 15 species in summer and can still name ten of them in midwinter with no leaves.
